correctness.rationale: For any connected simple G with n>=3 and minimum degree>=2, an inclusion-minimal connected vertex cover C of S(G) omits an independent set I of original vertices. Every subdivided cut edge incident to I is forced; selected subdivision vertices on edges of G-I must connect all retained originals and form a tree, since cycle edges are deletable. Conversely, any such I with G-I connected and spanning tree T gives a connected vertex cover C(I,T); the three original-vertex essentiality cases (omitted neighbor, unchosen incident internal edge, or tree degree>=2) use min degree 2 and establish full inclusion-minimality. The size is 2n-1+sum_(v in I)(deg_G(v)-2), and the sum of tau(G-I) yields the stated polynomial. For K_(2,q), summing over degree-two omissions gives q*3^(q-1), while omitting one high-degree vertex gives 2 at exponent 3q+1. Independent exact mask tests S(K4) produced 16 covers size 7 and 12 size 8; S(K2,3) produced 27 size 9 and 2 size 10; these match theorem. Infinite proof is structural.
